Competitive pressures and collective action problems together amplify AI risks by creating a situation where individual actors prioritize short-term gains over long-term safety investments. Competitive pressures lead companies to rush the development and deployment of AI systems to capture market advantages, often at the expense of thorough safety testing and risk mitigation. This "race to the bottom" dynamic results in all companies investing less in safety than they would prefer, as they feel compelled to match the reduced safety investments of competitors to maintain their market position.

Simultaneously, collective action problems prevent stakeholders from implementing safety measures that would benefit everyone. Even when there is a consensus on the need for certain safety measures, structural barriers and incentives to free-ride on others' investments hinder cooperation. This underinvestment in safety occurs despite the recognition of collective benefits, leading to a situation where the overall safety of AI systems is compromised, thereby increasing the likelihood and severity of harmful outcomes.
